1.why: verify-token requires the token's sessionId to match the caller's session and accountBinding to equal the fixed local account.

2.why: A reset token is bound to sessionId, so the same code is rejected when presented from a different session.

3.why: set-password updates the hash and flags only the current session; other sessions in the map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt and tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes, but nothing is encrypted at rest and plaintext test tokens are returned to the client.

6.why: There is no real email; API messages are generic, yet recovery tokens and links are returned in the JSON body for mock delivery.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/regex-validated and never interpolated into HTML; the page is a fixed template with only server nonce/CSRF substitution.

8.why: The only generated link is a same-origin path /?token=...; no open external redirects exist.

9.why: No email HTML templates are built from user input; delivery is mocked via local logs without embedding contact data as markup.

10.why: testToken, testLink, and mfaTestCode are returned by the API and appended to the on-page Logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but the MFA secret 482913 is hardcoded in source and returned to the client.

12.why: No default username/password pair or seeded credentials are defined; the account starts with an empty passwordHash.

13.why: Per-session limiters lock recovery/token/mfa/password categories after repeated failures for LOCK_MS (5 minutes).

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same ok message whether or not the contact is valid, avoiding account enumeration.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte crypto random values (base64url), short-lived, single-use, and bound to the requesting session/account.
